predecessors.note: Calakmul lies inside the Cliopatria 'Mayan City-States' envelope from 299.

land.text: 'the capital of a large regional state with an area of about 13,000 square kilometres'

successors.note: Calakmul stays inside Cliopatria's Later Mayan City-States shape until 1449; the site's elite presence lasts to about 900.

capitals.name: Calakmul (Ox Te' Tuun)
capitals.note: Coordinates 18 06' 19.41" N 89 48' 38.98" W from the page's infobox. The Kaan dynasty re-located here in the 7th century (earlier seat Dzibanche, page not loaded).

correction.text: Calakmul and its immediate land (Ox Te' Tuun)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row). Stela 114 (AD 435) 'probably records a 411 enthronement', the earliest evidence of a Calakmul dynasty; the page gives no size for the early kingdom, so a 25 km radius (the grid's minimum) is drawn. The Kaan dynasty 'was not originally established at Calakmul but rather re-located there in the 7th century' (from Dzibanche, page not loaded).

correction.text: 'the capital of a large regional state with an area of about 13,000 square kilometres'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'the capital of a large regional state with an area of about 13,000 square kilometres' (radius about 64 km), at its Late Classic height under Yuknoom Che'en II (636-c.686); 'governance at times reached places as far away as 150 kilometers'. The shape holds to the last stela (899 or 909) though the page says its power 'dwindled in the 8th century'.

region.text: Calakmul and its immediate land (Ox Te' Tuun)

ledger.note: About 411: a king is enthroned at Calakmul. Stela 114 (AD 435) 'probably records a 411 enthronement'; Calakmul was a Middle Preclassic site, and the page names Yuknoom Che'en I as a 5th-century ruler (dates uncertain).

region.text: Naranjo (Sa'al), whose king Aj Wosal was enthroned under Tuun K'ab' Hix in 546

ledger.note: 546: Calakmul's Tuun K'ab' Hix sets a king on Naranjo's throne. He 'oversaw the enthronement of Aj Wosal to the rulership of Naranjo in 546'; Calakmul 'was assembling a far-reaching political alliance' (the Snake Kingdom).

562: Calakmul defeats Tikal and takes Caracol as a dependency. 'Sky Witness defeated Tikal itself and sacrificed its king' in 562, and after 561 'He became the overlord of the city of Caracol', 'previously a Tikal vassal'.

About 622 (bridge; reviewer am-02 moved it from 618): the Calakmul page has 'King Yuknoom Chan of Calakmul supervised an event at Caracol in 619' and 'Caracol Stela 22 records the accession of Tajoom Uk'ab' K'ak' to the Calakmul throne in 622', so the overlordship lasted at least to 619; no page dates its end. The Caracol page has K'an II's 'ritual of alliance in Calakmul's territory' and Caracol attacking Naranjo in 627.

region.text: Naranjo (Sa'al), whose king Aj Wosal was enthroned under Tuun K'ab' Hix in 546

ledger.note: 626: Naranjo is free of Calakmul. Naranjo was 'independent of Calakmul by at least AD 626' (Caracol then attacked it, 627-631).

region.text: the regional state of about 13,000 km2 round Calakmul

ledger.note: 636: Yuknoom Che'en II comes to the throne and Calakmul reaches its height. 'Yuknoom Che'en II was 36 years old when he came to the throne of Calakmul in AD 636' and 'Calakmul experienced its highest achievements during the reign of king Yuknoom Che'en II'; the 13,000 km2 'regional state' is undated on the page, so the growth from the 25 km core is a bridging reading.

region.text: Dos Pilas, a vassal of Calakmul after 648

ledger.note: 648: Calakmul defeats Dos Pilas and makes it a vassal. 'Yuknoom Che'en II then reinstated Balaj Chan K'awiil upon the throne of Dos Pilas as his vassal' after he 'attacked and defeated Dos Pilas, capturing Balaj Chan K'awiil' (Tikal had founded Dos Pilas in 629).

region.text: Dos Pilas, a vassal of Calakmul after 648

ledger.note: 672: Tikal captures Dos Pilas and its king goes into exile, 'probably in Calakmul', ending the vassalage; the exile ended in 677 'on the same day that Calakmul celebrated a success over Tikal'.

region.text: 'the capital of a large regional state with an area of about 13,000 square kilometres'

ledger.note: About 909: the last Calakmul monument. Stela 61 'uses a shortened date form that is equivalent to a date either in 899 or 909, probably the latter'; 'political authority had already collapsed' by 830 yet 'there is strong evidence of an elite presence at the city continuing until AD 900, possibly even later'.

wars.name: Calakmul's wars on Palenque
wars.outcome: Uneh Chan attacked and sacked Palenque on 23 April 599 'with his ally Lakam Chak' and Calakmul sacked it again on 7 April 611; no territory is recorded as held.
wars.note: The Palenque page: 'troops from Calakmul invaded and sacked Palenque' (599) and 'A second victory by Calakmul occurred some twelve years later, in 611'.

wars.name: Calakmul-Caracol defeat of Tikal
wars.outcome: Sky Witness 'defeated Tikal itself and sacrificed its king' in 562; Caracol became Calakmul's dependency and Tikal entered a 130-year hiatus.
wars.note: Caracol's own text is damaged; the Tikal page dates the defeat to AD 562 at the hands of Calakmul and Caracol.

wars.name: Calakmul-Dos Pilas war

zones.text: Dos Pilas, a vassal of Calakmul after 648

wars.outcome: Calakmul defeated Dos Pilas in 648 and reinstated its king as a vassal; Tikal captured Dos Pilas in 672 and held it until 677.
wars.note: The Calakmul page adds 'Calakmul counterattacked in 677'.

wars.name: Tikal-Calakmul battle of 695
wars.outcome: In August 695 Tikal's Jasaw Chan K'awiil I defeated Yuknoom Yich'aak K'ak' in 'a catastrophic battle that saw the defeat of Calakmul'.
wars.note: The page makes this the start of Calakmul's decline in the 8th century; no border moves.

certainty.note: The kingdom had no fixed frontier; the 13,000 km2 regional state is a page figure for an undated Late Classic extent.

sources.title: Calakmul
sources.note: Kaan dynasty, Stela 114 (411), Naranjo 546, Caracol 561-562, Dos Pilas 648, 695, Stela 61 (899/909), 13,000 km2 regional state.

sources.title: Dos Pilas

notes:
NEW STATE. Cliopatria has no Calakmul row. Identity of the state: the page separates the site (Middle Preclassic to Late Classic) from the Kaan dynasty, which 'was not originally established at Calakmul but rather re-located there in the 7th century'; the Dzibanche page that would give the earlier seat did not load (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dzibanché, also tried percent-encoded), so the state is dated from the site's own 411 enthronement and the dynasty change is not a ledger event.
RADII. Only the 13,000 km2 'regional state' is a page figure and it is undated, so the 636 growth is confidence 1.
VASSALS WITHOUT DOSSIERS. Naranjo, Caracol (dossier written), El Peru-Waka' ('Yuknoom Che'en II oversaw the installation of K'inich B'alam as king'; defeated 743), Cancuen ('commanded the loyalty of three generations of kings', enthronements 656 and 677), Quirigua (sponsored rebellion 736-738); none dated well enough for a paired vassal event. A gap-filler could open El Peru and Cancuen.
THE 618 EVENT is a bridging judgement: the Caracol page shows an alliance ritual c. 618-620 but does not say the overlordship ended.
END. Stela 61 (899 or 909, 'probably the latter') is the last dated monument; Cliopatria's Later shape keeps the Calakmul area until 1449 and no page opened explains why.
